claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
Integrating graph neural networks with CALPHAD and first-principles calculations can accurately predict Young's modulus of HfNbTiVAl10.
Integrating graph neural networks with CALPHAD and first-principles calculations can accurately predict the yield strength of HfNbTiVAl10.
Integrating graph neural networks with CALPHAD and first-principles calculations can accurately predict the toughness of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed predictions apply under tensile and fracture testing.
Graph neural networks can learn complex relationships between chemical fluctuations, hierarchical heterostructure, and mechanical properties.
The integrated method will improve prediction accuracy relative to prior CALPHAD, first-principles, and machine-learning methods.
The integrated method will improve prediction efficiency relative to prior CALPHAD, first-principles, and machine-learning methods.
The method will cease to be reliable when chemical fluctuations or hierarchical heterostructure are not represented accurately.
The method will cease to be reliable when testing conditions fall outside the model's training range.
There is insufficient evidence to quantify expected gains in accuracy and efficiency.
The hypothesis would be falsified if prediction mean absolute error exceeds 10% of the experimental values.
